grades.quote: If a transaction aborts, the transaction processing system will read back through that transaction’s undo log entries, from the most recent to the earliest, and carry out each of the reversions listed in the log.
grades.reason: Background on undo logging (recording old values and reverting them), but it never discusses crash recovery or why repeating an undo must be safe (idempotency).

grades.quote: That way, recovery can read backward through the log, noting the completed transactions and processing the undo entries that are from other transactions.
grades.reason: Describes how recovery processes undo entries from a combined log, which is context for recovery. It doesn't say why undo must be safe to repeat.
About switching between threads. It has nothing to do with undo operations or crash recovery.

grades.quote: Idempotency is important if the system crashes after the undo record is written, but before the entity itself is written. Recovery processing can still “undo” the write that was never done. In addition, if the system crashes again in the middle of recovery, you can start it all over again from the beginning, without harm from repeated undo processing.
grades.reason: Directly explains that undo must be idempotent. A crash can happen after the undo record is written but before the entity is written, so recovery may "undo" a write that never happened. A crash during recovery can also force it to restart and repeat undo processing.
